title: Microsoft.Entra/roleAssignmentScheduleRequests
description: A PIM time-bound ACTIVE directory role assignment, shaped like ARM's Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignmentScheduleRequests. The resource name is a deterministic GUID chosen with guid() (a label, not the identity); the assignment is matched by (principalId, roleDefinitionId, directoryScopeId or appScopeId) and read live on every run. Created with action adminAssign, changed in place with adminUpdate, removed with adminRemove; justification and ticketInfo are request metadata, sent on every request and never compared. The schedule must be time-bound (AfterDateTime or AfterDuration): a permanent active assignment is Microsoft.Entra/roleAssignments, and the same principal, role and scope may not be declared by both. condition, conditionVersion and the target*/linked*ScheduleId properties of ARM are refused.

principalId.description: Required: object id of the user, role-assignable group or service principal the role is assigned to.

roleDefinitionId.description: The role template id (use roleTemplate('Display Name')), or use role. Not both.

role.description: EARM sugar: role template id, built-in role name, custom role display name or id; resolved to roleDefinitionId. Not with roleDefinitionId.

directoryScopeId.description: Scope: '/' (tenant, default), '/administrativeUnits/{id}' or '/{objectId}'. At most one of directoryScopeId, administrativeUnit and appScopeId.

administrativeUnit.description: EARM sugar for an administrative-unit scope: the unit's object id or its displayName; resolved to directoryScopeId.

appScopeId.description: An app-specific scope instead of a directory scope ('/' for tenant-wide app scopes).

requestType.description: Optional and only AdminAssign (any casing), so ARM snippets paste unchanged; EARM chooses adminAssign / adminUpdate / adminRemove itself.

scheduleInfo.description: Required: the assignment period, time-bound (NoExpiration is refused: use Microsoft.Entra/roleAssignments for a permanent assignment).

startDateTime.description: ISO 8601 start; absent or in the past means now (a past start is never drift).

type.description: AfterDateTime (needs endDateTime) or AfterDuration (needs duration); any casing, sent in Graph's camelCase. NoExpiration is refused.

endDateTime.description: AfterDateTime: the ISO 8601 end, after startDateTime. Compared with a 1 s tolerance.

duration.description: AfterDuration: an ISO 8601 duration such as P30D or PT8H. Applied when the assignment is created and never compared afterwards.

justification.description: Request metadata, sent on every request and never compared (default "Deployed by earm"); PIM policy may require it.

ticketInfo.description: Request metadata, sent on every request and never compared.

permissions.notes: Learn (rbacapplication-post-roleassignmentschedulerequests, rbacapplication-list-roleassignmentschedules): RoleAssignmentSchedule.ReadWrite.Directory is the least privileged permission for the requests (delegated and application); reads need RoleAssignmentSchedule.Read.Directory. Delegated callers need Privileged Role Administrator (Global Reader, Security Reader or Security Operator suffice for reads). Directory.Read.All covers the principal-kind check and the role / administrative unit name lookups. The tenant needs Microsoft Entra ID P2 or ID Governance.
